en.sup: Supplied in English. The Greek has only the article and the father's name in the genitive, 'the (one) of Alphaeus'.

01.n: Abbott-Smith lists four men of this name and puts this verse under the apostle.

03.n: Abbott-Smith derives the name from Aramaic בַּר־תָּלְמַי, 'son of Tolmai', and refers the reader to his entry for Nathanael.

04.n: Abbott-Smith derives the name from Hebrew תָּאוֹם, 'a twin', and compares the Greek δίδυμος.

06.r: The apostle called from the toll booth.
06.n: Abbott-Smith spells it Μαθθαῖος and notes that the received text spells it Ματθ-; a difference of spelling, not of name.

07.r: Marks the following word as the description that identifies him.

08.r: Matthew is named by the trade he left.
08.n: Abbott-Smith cites this verse under his second sense: a subordinate who collected taxes or tolls in a particular district (in the old English versions, 'publican'). This study renders it 'toll collector'. He is the only one in this list named by a trade; that the label recalls his former work is a reasonable reading.

09.r: The second apostle of this name, told apart by his father.
09.n: Abbott-Smith lists this verse under James the son of Alphaeus, and notes that he is commonly identified with James 'the little'.

10.r: The article stands for 'son', which the Greek leaves understood.

11.r: The article before the father's name; English does not use it.

12.n: Abbott-Smith gives the Aramaic form חַלְפַּי and keeps apart two men of this name: this one, the father of James, and another listed as the father of Levi.

17.n: Abbott-Smith gives Aramaic forms of the name and notes that in one place in Mark a marginal reading of Westcott and Hort has Λεββαῖος, Lebbaeus, instead.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus reads 'Lebbaeus, who was surnamed Thaddaeus' (Λεββαῖος ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Θαδδαῖος) where our text has 'Thaddaeus' alone. That is why the KJV, Geneva and YLT name Lebbeus first; the DRC, ASV and BSB have only Thaddaeus.
